title: Task 19A Decision Report: Zero-Fee Provider Onboarding and Local Secret Activation

decision.summary: Implement Task 19A as a capability-gated local portal that automatically configures admitted no-secret surfaces and resumes official provider-controlled credential or authorization flows. Do not claim universal automatic signup, universal zero-fee eligibility, or release readiness for every provider surface.
hard_blocks: FRED/ALFRED durable ingestion, persistence, modeling, export, and AI-facing use pending qualified rights resolution
Treasury daily-rate XML durable publication pending feed-specific rights admission
Coinbase and Kraken durable storage, modeling, and redistribution claims pending surface-specific rights evidence
provider OAuth, device authorization, and DCR until exact provider deployment and client eligibility are admitted
portable encrypted-fallback release claim until the existing repository vault passes independent Task 19A admission review
any active provider or OS-backend claim until bounded runtime evidence exists
conditional_gates: BLS activation requires exact provenance, access-date citation, disclaimer, truthful-representation, limit-compliance, third-party-rights scope, and bounded runtime evidence
SEC and Fiscal Data activation require bounded runtime evidence despite documentation-ready no-secret status

scope.topic: Zero-fee provider onboarding portal for Market Squawk: official user authorization, account and API credential issuance, local secret activation, and automation boundaries

principles: Semantically deduplicate completed batch and category evidence rather than concatenate reports.
Use primary provider, government, IETF, and operating-system sources.
Keep endpoint accessibility, price evidence, credential authority, data-use rights, and runtime readiness as independent decisions.
Bind mutable provider evidence to retrieval time, digest, and refresh trigger.
Distinguish confirmed source facts, formal or empirical results, engineering inferences, and project architecture requirements.
Use GitHub exact-commit evidence only for implementation fit, never for provider capability or rights.
methodology.source_lineage_resolution: The canonical root inventory contains 60 selected first-class sources, 17 explicit exclusions, seven batch assignments, per-source access state, and digest or stable-reference metadata. Four canonical category syntheses feed the final report.

implementation_context.origin: project context supplied for Task 19A; not an external research finding
implementation_context.decision: Independently audit and admit the existing implementation against the complete fallback criteria. Do not invent a replacement cryptosystem unless the existing candidate fails with documented evidence.
implementation_context.external_research_limitation: The reviewed external sources did not select or validate a portable encrypted-vault construction.

cross_source_invariants: A surface becomes ActiveScoped only after provider capability, human boundary, runtime, least privilege, secure storage when needed, rate, and rights admissions all pass.
NoCredential, free, and durable-use rights are separate fields.
Runtime metadata can narrow but not broaden the adapter's reviewed capabilities.
Credential capture or secure storage never equals permission or rights verification.
Remote provider validity and local possession are separate systems of record.
Cancellation prevents later activation but cannot prove external side effects were rolled back.
Secret bytes and one-time authorization material never enter SQLite, analytical storage, logs, MCP results, command lines, URLs, or durable audit.
All onboarding and secret operations remain outside the live event-to-action path.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Every provider surface has a versioned evidence-backed capability record with setup, human boundary, authority, verifier, rate, rights, lifecycle, source digests, and refresh trigger; runtime metadata can only narrow it.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Catalog/config schema and focused invariant evidence for all ten surfaces.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Expose five distinct setup modes and hide or mark unsupported provider modes; no generic library may create a provider capability.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: End-to-end service, CLI, and portal state evidence.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Provider-controlled steps use durable UserActionRequired/resume with exact official deep link and permissions; cancellation cannot loop or fabricate completion.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Focused manual, browser, and device state-transition evidence.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Coinbase public asks for no secret; private requires view and expected portfolio and rejects trade, transfer, and receive.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Bounded authorized permission evidence with redacted audit.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Kraken public asks for no secret; private enforces an exact query-only key-info profile and redacts sensitive response fields.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Bounded authorized key-info evidence and exact permission comparison.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: SEC uses no credential, declared User-Agent identity/contact, one aggregate limiter at or below current 10/s, semantic probe, and scoped EDGAR rights lineage.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Known-CIK/accession smoke, limiter evidence, and rights record.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: FRED cannot activate persistence, modeling, export, or AI-facing use without qualified scope-bound rights admission and required permissions; a valid key never bypasses the gate.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Service-boundary denial evidence, rights schema, and refreshed terms digest.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: BLS v1 enforces all lower-tier limits. BLS v2 requires human registration/key import, enforces higher-tier limits, tracks at-least-annual renewal, and never assumes anonymous v2. Both bind exact BLS provenance, access-date citation, required disclaimer, truthful representation, limit compliance, and third-party-rights boundaries.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Exact quota and renewal policy, terms-duty record, scope rejection, and bounded semantic runtime evidence.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Treasury XML validates bounded anonymous XML and remains rights-blocked; Fiscal Data validates anonymous response metadata and binds license to exact dataset provenance.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Two bounded smokes and distinct rights records.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Native OAuth cannot enable without provider public-client, redirect, issuer/endpoints, PKCE S256, scope, and refresh-replay admission; it uses external browser and one exact callback consumption.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Focused protocol state tests and provider capability fixture.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Device flow cannot enable without provider support and honors interval, default, slow_down, timeout backoff, expiry, cancellation, explicit restart, and durable redaction.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Deterministic protocol-state and redaction evidence.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: DCR/RFC7592 remains disabled without exact provider support; mutating timeout becomes indeterminate; registration credentials go directly to secure storage; UI never calls DCR account creation.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Capability gate, reconciliation, secret routing, and terminology review.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Apple, Windows, and Secret Service backends provide exact CRUD, probe, prompt/cancel/deadline, and typed failures without flattening platform states.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Focused validation on every claimed OS/backend including locked and headless states.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Independently admit the existing market-squawk-platform::secrets vault for Argon2id, XChaCha20-Poly1305, key custody, capability confinement, crash consistency, generations, rotation/recovery, corruption, migration/backup, rollback, permissions, and no plaintext fallback; invent a replacement only after documented failure.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Exact-commit code/design review, focused format/invariant tests, fault injection, migration fixture, and threat-model decision.
acceptance_criteria.context_note: Repository implementation context, not externally validated evidence.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Only opaque SecretRef and non-secret metadata may enter catalog/log/artifact/MCP; all credential and one-time authorization material is excluded.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Targeted success/failure persistence, logging, audit, and MCP inspection.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Store/catalog activation is generation-bound and crash-recoverable with exact selectors and orphan reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Fault injection at each boundary and idempotent restart evidence.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Permission verification records requested versus observed authority and required bindings; missing or excess authority fails closed.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Focused exact, missing, excess, mismatch, expiry, and semantic-error cases.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Rotation/revocation separates replacement, verification, cutover, remote result, local deletion, retirement, and cleanup; local delete is never shown as confirmed remote revoke.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: State-machine and crash-recovery evidence for overlapping and revoke-first orders.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Every browser, device, provider, prompt/store, and cleanup operation has one owner, monotonic deadline, cancellation, terminal state, and bounded retry; cancellation cannot erase indeterminate side effects.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Focused cancellation/deadline tests and no orphan worker/listener evidence.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Audit records actor, opaque IDs/generations, revisions, human boundary, non-secret authority summary, deadlines, timestamps, and lifecycle results without secret material or echoing raw errors.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Redaction evidence on success, failure, cancellation, and provider-error paths.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Rate policy is provider/product/protocol/endpoint/version specific, enforces every dimension, treats unknown conservatively, and refreshes on 429 or evidence change. Separately, the Market Squawk project requires heartbeat/connection health never to masquerade as market-data freshness.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Policy fixtures and bounded runtime observations; no unlimited default.
acceptance_criteria.project_requirement_note: The heartbeat-versus-market-freshness clause is internal project architecture, not externally established by provider pages.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Rights admission binds exact source/surface/dataset/version, terms digest/time, operations, retention, derivatives, modeling/export/redistribution, attribution, third-party rights, reviewer, and refresh trigger. BLS preserves affirmative secondary-use evidence and its duties; network success cannot bypass any rights decision.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Rights registry and service-boundary evidence for FRED hard denial, scoped BLS admission/duties, Treasury XML and exchange unknowns, and Fiscal Data provenance.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Separately authorized bounded runtime smokes prove every claimed provider and OS-backend capability; deterministic default tests remain offline.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Exact-commit, time-bound, redacted semantic smoke artifacts.

acceptance_criteria.requirement: Onboarding, OAuth, MCP, catalog, persistence, and secure-store work stays outside the live event-to-action path; no consumer can use authority below ActiveScoped.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Architecture trace and focused authority-boundary evidence.
acceptance_criteria.project_requirement_note: Hot-path exclusion and ActiveScoped authority are Market Squawk requirements; external sources neither establish nor replace them.

conflicts.description: BLS newer FAQ requires v2 registration while older examples omit a key.
conflicts.resolution: Require the key and treat anonymous v2 as unknown.

conflicts.description: Fiscal Data says no token is required while its 403 description mentions an invalid API key.
conflicts.resolution: Do not invent a key; monitor bounded anonymous behavior.

conflicts.description: SEC API and filing delays describe distinct paths and are not service-level guarantees.
conflicts.resolution: Track endpoint class and observed freshness separately.

conflicts.description: FRED short permission summaries cannot override broader storage, AI/ML, attribution, and third-party content terms.
conflicts.resolution: Keep durable use blocked pending qualified scope-specific admission.

conflicts.description: Exact OAuth redirects and variable native loopback ports appear to conflict.
conflicts.resolution: Only the registered literal-loopback port may vary; every other component remains exact.

conflicts.description: Credential Manager local-machine persistence and DPAPI CRYPTPROTECT_LOCAL_MACHINE have different access semantics.
conflicts.resolution: Use same-user persistence and reject the broader DPAPI flag as the per-user default.

conflicts.description: BLS affirmative secondary-use language coexists with attribution/disclaimer, truthful-representation, limit-compliance, and third-party-rights duties.
conflicts.resolution: Bind both permission signal and duties to exact BLS provenance and requested operations; do not represent BLS as a pure rights non-finding or a blanket grant.

gaps.description: FRED qualified rights resolution and any required written permissions.
Coinbase/Kraken surface-specific storage, modeling, and reuse rights evidence.
Treasury XML feed-specific rights evidence; BLS uses outside the scoped official terms/provenance record require separate admission.
Independent admission of the existing market-squawk-platform::secrets vault at the candidate commit.
Exact provider OAuth, device, DCR, introspection, revocation, and refresh replay support where requested.
Bounded provider and supported-platform runtime smokes.
Measured browser, provider, prompt, store, and cleanup deadlines.

explicit_non_findings: No official evidence establishes universal automatic provider account or personal API-key creation.
No generally available retail Coinbase/Kraken device flow or DCR capability is admitted.
No universal zero-fee commitment is established for every Coinbase/Kraken activity or private account.
No provider or platform runtime behavior was observed during this research.
No source proves local deletion remotely revokes a provider credential.
No cross-platform secure-store equivalence is established.
No external source validates the existing Market Squawk encrypted vault implementation.

category_evidence.finding: Maintained implementation candidates exist for typed Rust OAuth and native stores; repository evidence does not establish provider capability, rights, or release fitness.
OAuth composition and cross-app differentiation require complete participant and transaction binding; the papers do not directly evaluate Market Squawk or provider support.

Least privilege, no provider-password collection, complete secret lifecycle, redacted audit, user intent, and provenance-specific rights records are cross-provider controls; guidance does not override provider terms.
